prompts.name: create-from-workflow
prompts.prompt: I keep doing the same tedious thing every sprint and I want to stop. When we cut a release, I manually: pull the merged PRs since the last tag, group them by conventional-commit type, check which ones touched the public API, draft the changelog section with breaking changes highlighted, bump the version, and tag. It takes me 40 minutes and I always forget the API-change check. Turn this into a Hermes skill so the agent does it next time. I care about: it should trigger when I say things like "cut the release", "draft the changelog", or "prepare the next version"; it must never push or tag without me seeing the drafted changelog first; and it should produce a markdown changelog block I can paste into the release notes. Give me a couple of realistic test cases too, and write the skill under a `release` category.

expectations.text: A skill directory is created under a 'release' category with a SKILL.md whose name matches its directory
SKILL.md frontmatter contains name, a trigger-action description, and tags
The description encodes the trigger phrases ("cut the release", "draft the changelog", "prepare the next version")
The skill body includes a safety rule requiring human review of the drafted changelog before any push or tag
The skill declares the public-API-change check as an explicit workflow step
A test-case file is created with at least two realistic prompts
The captured workflow genuinely removes the manual 40-minute routine rather than restating it

prompts.name: evaluate-and-improve
prompts.prompt: I drafted this skill for extracting tables out of PDFs into CSV and I think it's OK but I've never actually checked whether it works. Here's the SKILL.md at `/home/hermes-user/workspace/drafts/pdf-table-extract/SKILL.md`. Can you test it properly and improve it? I want to know whether the skill actually helps versus just asking the model cold, not a gut feeling. If it's bad, make it better and show me the before/after.

expectations.text: A workspace is created as a sibling of the skill directory, organised by iteration
Each eval has a with-skill configuration and a without-skill (baseline) configuration, with more than one run each
A grading record is written per run using the field names text, passed, and evidence
An aggregated benchmark.json (and benchmark.md) exists with pass_rate per configuration and the delta
An HTML eval viewer is generated from the workspace and its path delivered to the user
At least one iteration of improvement is applied and rerun into a later iteration directory
No evaluation record claims more than was measured (no all-green 'complete' status for an unrun suite)
The improvement is general rather than overfit to the specific test prompts

prompts.name: port-align-upstream
prompts.prompt: I've got a Hermes skill called `web-perf-audit` that I wrote from scratch, and I've since found that the `webapp-testing` skill in `anthropics/skills` does a much more thorough job of driving a browser for audits. I'd like to align mine with theirs — pull in what's genuinely better without wrecking the Hermes-specific bits (it uses the `delegate_task` runner and Hermes frontmatter keys). Be careful: theirs shells out to a Node/Playwright CLI I don't want to depend on. Show me what you'd change and why before doing it.

expectations.text: The upstream is inspected and its real capabilities verified before design (commands, files) rather than assumed
Each upstream artefact is classified as engine-agnostic (portable) or engine-coupled (rewrite)
Engine-coupled pieces that shell out to a non-Hermes CLI are rewritten rather than copied verbatim
The Hermes-specific choices already in the skill (delegate_task runner, Hermes frontmatter keys) are preserved
Divergences from upstream are recorded in an HTML comment at the end of SKILL.md
The proposed changes are presented to the user before being applied
The result is a selective port, not a wholesale replacement, and stays coherent as a Hermes skill
